title: input_parity_right_click scenario claims to pin the W3/W5 right-click select but asserts nothing about it
evidence: parity.odin:523-525: "// 11. right_click — mouse: draw 0->1, right-click the pipe SELECTS it (the / W3/W5 transcription, wired through a minimal parity effect that mirrors / the app's effect_right_click) — no commands, sel_pipe == 0." check_states (parity.odin:671-696) switches only on "input_parity_select", "input_parity_tier_cycle", "input_parity_class_cycle", "input_parity_cancel", "input_parity_pan" — no right_click case; the scenario's script is mouse-only (parity.odin:528-533, `mouse = frames(...)`, no touch/pad), so cross-device equality in check_scenario is vacuous, and run_input_parity gates check_manifest on `sc.name == "input_parity_draw" || sc.name == "input_parity_draw_wide"` only.
detail: The golden's own comment promises the right-click SELECT is pinned, but only the command stream is asserted (the draw). A right-click that selects the wrong pipe, misses the select, or fails the drag interrupt passes the golden — the W3/W5 transcription is unpinned.
recommended_fix: Add an input_parity_right_click case to check_states asserting the run's sel_pipe == 0, sel_node == -1, drag cleared, and press_swallowed set after the right press.

title: parity_right_click_effect hand-duplicates app/main.odin's effect_right_click instead of sharing one executor proc
evidence: parity.odin:109-113: "// parity_right_click_effect — the right-click select path (the app's / effect_right_click body, wired into the parity ctx so the right-click / scenario pins the W3/W5 transcription: the drag interrupt + the pipe / select). Mirrors app/main.odin's effect_right_click exactly." Body: "wx, wy := rnd.from_screen(ictx.view, pos.x, pos.y) ... if pid, ok := inp.pipe_hit(ictx.topo, ictx.cat, wx, wy); ok { ictx.sel_pipe = i64(pid); ictx.sel_node = -1; ictx.sel_class = 0; ictx.qos_editing = false }" — identical to main.odin:625-641's effect_right_click body (same lines, `app.input.*` derefs). exec.odin:11-13 establishes the opposite pattern: "The world-hit helpers (snap_node, pipe_hit, tile math) move here from app/main.odin with EXPLICIT args (topo/cat/view) — pure reads, usable by the app's render-side code and the harness parity test alike."
detail: The one transcribed behavior the PR did NOT move into the shared executor is exactly the one the harness had to copy. The golden pins the copy, not the app's real handler; the two bodies must be hand-synced and drift silently decays the parity guarantee.
recommended_fix: Move the right-click body into app/input/exec.odin with explicit args (the established snap_node/click_select pattern), have effect_right_click delegate to it, and wire parity_right_click_effect to the shared proc.
